judgment.rationale: A maintainer confirmed the reported contrast-theme failure on PowerToys 0.78, and the issue includes a concrete sequence. The current Image Resizer uses WinUI theme resources, but its implementation differs from the original 0.77 report and has not been verified on a current release; treat theme propagation as a likely, not confirmed, fix direction.
evidence: The reporter described a custom Windows contrast-theme sequence and said Image Resizer remained light while other PowerToys surfaces changed.
A maintainer confirmed reproduction on PowerToys 0.78.

The current App.xaml loads XamlControlsResources and MainWindow.xaml uses ThemeResource; MainWindow.xaml.cs calls TitleBarHelper.SetPreferredTheme for the title bar, with no explicit Image Resizer high-contrast synchronization found in the inspected app/window path.
judgment.recommended_action: Repeat the documented contrast-theme sequence on a current stable release before selecting a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: No code change is justified until the historical contrast-theme failure is verified on the current release.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says a customized Windows contrast theme applies to other PowerToys surfaces but Image Resizer remains light; a maintainer reproduced it on PowerToys 0.78.
known_information: The original report was filed against PowerToys 0.77.0 and includes steps for customizing a Windows contrast theme and switching to it.
The reporter later supplied a more detailed sequence, and a maintainer confirmed the issue on 0.78.
The issue is currently open, unassigned, and labeled Status-Reproducible.
inferences: The symptom may be caused by Image Resizer content not following the active contrast palette, but current WinUI resource behavior has not been verified on the current release.
issue_context.analysis: The issue has enough history to avoid a generic log request. The best next step is to establish whether it persists in the current release; if so, inspect the app/window theme-resource transition rather than assuming the title-bar helper controls all content.
initial_investigation: Inspected the Image Resizer app and window theme setup and the historical discussion. No current-release reproduction was performed.

information_gaps.information: Whether the supplied sequence still reproduces, and the PowerToys version used for that confirmation.
information_gaps.why_needed: The current app implementation may differ from the version where the maintainer reproduced the issue.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the supplied contrast-theme sequence on the current stable release and include the About PowerToys version.

information_gaps.information: The Windows version and build used for the current or most recent reproduction.
information_gaps.why_needed: Contrast-theme behavior and WinUI system integration can vary by Windows build.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Include the Windows edition, version, and OS build from Settings > System > About.

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed reproduction steps and for confirming this on PowerToys 0.78. Could you please:
- confirm whether the same sequence still reproduces on a current PowerToys release and include the PowerToys version you tested;
- share the Windows edition, version, and OS build from Settings > System > About.
That will tell us whether the current Image Resizer theme path remains affected or whether the reported behavior was specific to the earlier implementation.

actions.label: Reproduce current Image Resizer contrast behavior
actions.note: The report includes a concrete sequence and maintainer confirmation on 0.78; verify whether the current implementation still fails before finalizing a fix.

reproduce.title: Verify Image Resizer with a customized Windows contrast theme
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys release; compare with the reported 0.77 and maintainer-confirmed 0.78 behavior if available
prerequisites: Use an isolated Windows test environment with Contrast themes available.
Enable Image Resizer and use a test image.
setup: Enable a built-in contrast theme, then customize its cursor style and wallpaper and save it as a custom theme, following the reporter's sequence.
steps: Switch to the saved custom contrast theme using Shift+Alt+PrintScreen.
Open an image in PowerToys Image Resizer and compare the content and title bar with other Windows and PowerToys surfaces.
Switch to another contrast theme and back while Image Resizer is open; then close and reopen Image Resizer.
Record whether the Image Resizer content follows the selected contrast palette at each step.
reproduce.expected_result: Image Resizer content and title bar use the active customized contrast palette and update when the selected contrast theme changes or the app is reopened.
